messages.subject: Re: add jar packages to classPath from a directory
messages.subject_clean: add jar packages to classPath from a directory
messages.body_plain:
Joe,

that's actually trivially done directly with rJava  and R with arbitrarily many paths via

.jaddClassPath(Sys.glob("/foo/bar/*.jar","/foo/new/*.jar"))

Cheers,
Simon


> On Feb 10, 2017, at 7:55 AM, Joe W. Byers <ecjbosu at aol.com> wrote:
> 
> I found when using rJava to scrape data from web pages and other task where java had packages the R does not, I needed to load multiple jars to the classpath.  This was tedious to code and maintain  I created the following method to load all jar files in a directory.  This made my life significantly easier when I had automated tasks and building new rJava applications.   I wanted to share it with you and if the team wants,  please include this in the package.
> 
> Have a great day.
> Joe
> #' ==============================================================================
> #' Name   : setJarClasses
> #' Author : Joe W. Byers
> #' Date   : 08/13/2014
> #' Version: 1.0001
> #' Aim    : add jar packages to classPath from a directory.  Default dir = /usr/share/java
> #' Mail   : <<<ecjbosu at aol.com>>>
> #' License: GPL-3
> #' ==============================================================================
> 
> setJarClasses <-function (jardir='/usr/share/java'){
> require(rJava);
> 
> .jinit()
> #load jars
> #jar directory
> #put in a system cache database
> jarfiles = list.files(jardir, all.files = F, full.names = T, include.dirs=F);
> 
> ret=lapply(jarfiles, function(x) .jaddClassPath(x));
> ret = .jclassPath();
> 
> #detach("package:rJava");
> return(ret);
> 
> }                                         
> 
> -- 
> Joe W. Byers

messages.body_plain:
Prashant,

> On May 18, 2017, at 6:41 AM, Prashant Choudhary <prashant_choudhary at scmhrd.edu> wrote:
> 
> Hello All,
> 
> i want to integrate R with Java. I am trying to print R data summaries in Java but it is not working. Please help
> 
>  RList desc = c.eval("list(summary(mpg))").asList();
>  System.out.println(desc);
> 

println can only print strings - so you either get the summary object and then you have to write the Java code to access the pieces, or you use capture.output(print(...)) in R and fetch the string in Java if you want to print it.

Cheers,
Simon
